entries.title: Three Iran-backed suspects plotted attacks including RAF Fairford incident, US says

entries.snippet: Supporters of Sheikh Hasina want her to return from exile in India.

entries.snippet: Real Madrid player Vinícius Jr sent a surprise message to 13-year-old fan Zaher who lost both his legs after being hit by a drone in Khartoum, in 2024.

entries.snippet: Slovyansk continues to be bombarded by Russian forces, making it almost uninhabitable with less than 10% of its pre-war population remaining.

entries.title: 'It can kill us': Kenyans fear impact of El Niño with floods predicted
entries.snippet: Forecasters warn that this year's El Niño could be one of the strongest on record, with heavy rain and flooding in Kenya.

entries.snippet: Iran-backed operatives have been charged over nearly 20 attacks, including a plot on a U.K. base housing U.S. troops. Separately, a U.S. soldier is held in the U.K. on Russia spying claims.

entries.title: Oil giant ExxonMobil left Venezuela years ago. Now it's considering a return
entries.snippet: ExxonMobil has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Venezuelan government and its state-owned oil company to explore opportunities in the country.

entries.title: AI hoaxes are deceiving 911 dispatchers, and they're only getting harder to detect
entries.snippet: Swatters are increasingly using AI technology that creates synthetic voices or sound effects to generate remarkably believable fake emergency calls to law enforcement.

entries.title: Volunteer musicians play songs for veterans who are hospitalized
entries.snippet: Volunteer musicians play for veterans and others who are hospitalized. They're part of Musicians On Call, a group that spreads the healing power of music.

entries.title: Both sides now? Critics slam DOJ moves to dismiss convictions of Trump allies
entries.snippet: The DOJ moved to dismiss criminal convictions of former Trump adviser Steve Bannon and of the Oath Keepers, in what it calls "the interests of justice." Critics are crying foul.

entries.title: Your guide to hosting a flavorful, cozy and stress-free Thanksgiving
entries.snippet: Whether you're hosting friendsgiving or Thanksgiving, we've got foolproof turkey recipes, advice on how to stay present while hosting, and directions on how to create a stunning floral arrangement.

entries.title: U.S. officials look to Europe to learn how to make prison better
entries.snippet: American prison officials are looking to European nations like Germany and Norway for a roadmap on how to design a prison that emphasizes rehabilitation and a successful return to life on the outside.

entries.title: Spain's first general strike in 14 years demands solutions to housing crisis
entries.snippet: Less than three weeks before a national election that could catapult the far right to power, Spain's workers are striking on Wednesday to demand that the government remedy the nation's housing crisis.

entries.snippet: Eighteen states run by Democrats have already joined an interstate compact to award their Electoral College votes to whichever presidential candidate wins the national popular vote.

entries.snippet: Authorities suspect him of assisting a foreign intelligence service and obtaining or disclosing protected information.

entries.snippet: Jean Léonard Teganya arrived in the East African nation on Monday, and Rwandan prosecutors said they will put him on trial for alleged genocide and crimes against humanity.

entries.title: At UN climate talks, 5 nations back plan to double rooftop solar panels by 2030
entries.snippet: Five countries have backed a plan to double the number of homes with rooftop solar panels worldwide by 2030, as U.N. climate talks in Turkey focus on expanding access to electricity and transitioning away from fossil fuels.

entries.title: California voters reject tax on net worth of billionaires
entries.snippet: The measure would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion.

entries.title: British comedian and children's author David Walliams accused of sexual misconduct
entries.snippet: An investigation by ITV News and the Guardian revealed multiple accusations, including one of sexual assault of a 15-year-old. Walliams has denied the claims, stating, "I am not a sexual predator."

entries.title: Iran classes Argentina navy, air force as 'terrorist organizations'
entries.snippet: In a tit-for-tat move, Iran has said it now considers Argentina's navy and air force as "terrorist organizations." Tehran claimed Buenos Aires is responsible for further consequences.

entries.title: Spain: Housing crisis prompts general strike
entries.snippet: Workers across nearly all industries have taken to the picket lines as rents soar and the housing crunch worsens. The crisis is the main political debate ahead of Spain's November 29 elections.

entries.title: DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's important.
entries.snippet: Doing nothing might be the ultimate brain hack. When you're bored, the brain goes into default mode network. It's not only healthy for you, but it may also shape the very essence of your identity.

entries.title: India: CPCB addresses stark Delhi pollution data gap on Diwali night
entries.snippet: India's main pollution monitor has issued a clarification on a wide air quality data gap between official and private reporting in New Delhi that saw the city choked amid Diwali fireworks. DW has the latest.

entries.title: Germany slips in climate protection rankings as other countries make gains
entries.snippet: Record renewable energy growth is driving climate progress in some countries, but Germany and many major emitters are falling behind.

entries.title: How AI worsens online violence against Middle East women
entries.snippet: Women in the Middle East already have to deal with an above-average share of online harassment and violence. The proliferation of AI-enabled tools is making it worse.

entries.title: South Korea bus causes large crash near Seoul, dozens hurt
entries.snippet: The bus triggered a collision involving more than 30 vehicles, including other buses, during rush hour traffic in the South Korean city of Seongnam, just south of Seoul.

entries.title: Israel: Eisenkot proposes October 7 probe as new Knesset sworn in
entries.snippet: Ex-IDF chief Gadi Eisenkot has yet to forge a coalition that would allow him to replace Benjamin Netanyahu, despite the new Knesset being dominated by the critics of the current prime minister.

entries.title: US Republicans derail push to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
entries.snippet: Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth seems set to survive the impeachment bid launched by maverick Republican lawmaker Thomas Massie, with President Donald Trump praising the outcome of the vote.

entries.title: US charges 3 alleged Iranian operatives over plots targeting Jewish communities and a UK airbase
entries.snippet: US prosecutors claim the three men were planning a "campaign of terror" against Jewish communities and a UK airbase. The Fairford incident prompted the US to pull out its bombers used for operations against Iran.

entries.title: Former Malaysian leader Najib Razak returns home under royal pardon, but faces a separate 15-year prison sentence
entries.snippet: Najib Razak has left prison under a royal pardon, prompting a minister to resign in protest. Malaysia's former leader still faces a separate 15-year sentence over the corruption scandal that brought him down.

entries.title: British counterterrorism police arrest US soldier accused of spying on behalf of Russia
entries.snippet: A member of the US Army has been arrested near Gloucester in England. Police said he was suspected of espionage activity in connection with Russia. Investigators from the US and UK are involved in the probe.

entries.title: UK Privy Council overrules Trinidad and Tobago gay sex law
entries.snippet: A London court has overturned a Trinidad and Tobago law criminalizing consensual sexual relations between male same-sex couples. As a result of the colonial legacy, it is the independent country's last court of appeal.

entries.title: Victims of Nazi war in Poland call on Germany for support
entries.snippet: More than 80 years after the end of World War II, Polish victims of the Nazi regime are still waiting for a "humanitarian gesture" from Germany. The 2027 draft budget hasn't left them much hope for possible reparations.

entries.title: Iran denies role in fridge hack, France summons ambassador
entries.snippet: France has said it rules "nothing" out in response to a cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration units. Iran, however, said it categorically rejected Paris' "baseless and one-sided accusations" of IRGC involvement.

entries.title: Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?
entries.snippet: Hitler once called Eastern Europe "Germany's India." A new exhibition examines the links between colonialism and Nazism, and the bitter debate over where comparisons illuminate history and where they fall short.

entries.title: Poland: Krakow shooting suspect 'fascinated' by Norwegian mass murder Anders Breivik, says justice minister
entries.snippet: The 24-year old suspect was found to have read a significant amount of material about Breivik and other far-right figures. Speculation over his motives have prompted a bitter political feud in Warsaw.

entries.title: Neuer injury gives Urbig chance to shape Bayern and Germany future
entries.snippet: Manuel Neuer's latest injury gives Jonas Urbig a run of games in Bayern's goal. Marc-André ter Stegen remains Germany’s No. 1, but Urbig now has a chance to strengthen his case for the future.

entries.title: Megaspeed and the battle to go high-end Nvidia chips into China
entries.snippet: Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy has shone a light on Megaspeed, the company she worked for. It is under investigation in the US for smuggling Nvidia chips into China, which it denies.
